sources.design: Final evidence-based clinical practice guideline; not a single intervention trial.
sources.population: Clinically diagnosed midportion Achilles tendinopathy; recommendation excludes presumed tendon frailty.
sources.comparator: Multiple heterogeneous evidence comparisons, including wait-and-see and loading alternatives.
sources.coInterventions: Education recommended with loading; adjunct choices vary.
sources.outcomes: Tendon loading first-line (grade A); final frequency at least 3/week (grade E). Complete rest not indicated; activity within pain tolerance. No universally superior loading type.
sources.followUp: Heterogeneous primary follow-up; no single guideline endpoint.
sources.uncertainty: Frequency is an expert recommendation, not proof of an optimal numeric threshold. Insertional pathology outside scope.
sources.limitations: Frequency is an expert recommendation, not proof of an optimal numeric threshold. Insertional pathology outside scope. Research candidate only; no clinical release.

protocol.supervision: Clinician-delivered education; supervision not fixed for one universal protocol.
protocol.progression: Individual pain tolerance/functional capacity; no universal increment.
protocol.stoppingRules: No universal stopping threshold; guideline advises activity within pain tolerance.

sources.design: Randomised trial, 58 randomised; attrition and last-observation-carried-forward analysis.
sources.population: Recreational athletes with chronic >3-month unilateral midportion Achilles tendinopathy, age eligibility 18–60; insertional disease excluded.
sources.comparator: Heavy slow resistance versus eccentric loading.
sources.coInterventions: Instruction/manual, initial physiotherapist demonstration and 1-week check; initial sport restriction then monitored activity.
sources.outcomes: VISA-A/pain improved in both at 12 and 52 weeks, no between-group superiority. HSR adherence 92% versus 78%.
sources.uncertainty: Small sample, no untreated comparator; no inference that eccentric loading caused rupture. Full-ROM protocol not insertional evidence.
sources.harms: One eccentric-arm partial rupture during badminton; HSR withdrawals included ankle/back pain; causality not established.
sources.limitations: Small sample, no untreated comparator; no inference that eccentric loading caused rupture. Full-ROM protocol not insertional evidence. Research candidate only; no clinical release.

protocol.execution: HSR bilateral seated bent-knee machine raise, straight-knee leg-press raise and barbell-on-shoulders raise with forefoot on disc; full ankle ROM. Comparator unilateral straight/bent-knee eccentric heel lowering on step.
protocol.dose: HSR: 3 × 15RM week 1; 3 × 12RM weeks 2–3; 4 × 10RM weeks 4–5; 4 × 8RM weeks 6–8; 4 × 6RM weeks 9–12. Three seconds each concentric/eccentric phase; 2–3-minute rests. Eccentric comparator: each exercise 3 × 15 with approximately three-second lowering.
protocol.frequency: HSR three times weekly for 12 weeks; eccentric exercises twice daily, seven days weekly.
protocol.supervision: Physiotherapist instruction and follow-up after one week; training diary thereafter.
protocol.progression: Increasing load with decreasing RM schedule; eccentric backpack load increased as pain diminished.
protocol.stoppingRules: Study allowed exercise VAS 40–50 mm if settled by next session. Sport was withheld for the first three weeks, then discomfort limited to 30 mm. These are trial-specific values, not app thresholds.
